amendments.body: crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:555-556 still hardcodes `let temp_factor = raw_temp_factor.max(0.25);` inside `molt_cycle`, even though crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1611-1620 and crates/tank_data/data/shrimp/neocaridina_davidi.toml:164-171 now make the temperature floor species-configurable via `temp_condition_min_factor`. Any preset value below `0.25` changes condition/success scoring but has no effect on molt cadence, so the new parameter is only partially effective and the model still hides a thermal timing constant. Either parameterize the cadence floor separately or use the named floor consistently when computing `effective_interval`.
amendments.rationale: This leaves a hidden constant in the exact pathway the new parameter was supposed to expose, so species tuning can silently fail to change molt timing.

amendments.body: Validation for `temp_condition_min_factor` disagrees across data entry paths: crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:981-1005 rejects `0.0` by treating the field as strictly positive, while crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:466-469 accepts `0.0` with `check_unit_interval`. As a result, a runtime/save-state configuration can legally use `0.0`, but the equivalent species preset cannot be authored or round-tripped through the preset layer. Align the lower bound across preset validation, runtime invariants, and tests/docs.
amendments.rationale: The same parameter should not have different legal domains depending on whether it comes from a preset file or a saved simulation; that is a configuration correctness and maintenance risk.

payload.summary: Review found two issues in the new temperature-floor parameterization: molt timing still has a hidden hardcoded `0.25` floor that overrides the new species setting, and the preset/runtime validators disagree on whether `temp_condition_min_factor = 0.0` is legal.
